adjudication_label: MD simulation interface modeling and structural definition
canonical_question: How is the interface between the FeNiCrCoCu coating and the Cu matrix modeled in the simulation?

question_variants.question: How is the interface between the FeNiCrCoCu coating and the Cu matrix modeled in the simulation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The interface is modeled using single crystal FCC structures for both the FeNiCrCoCu coating and the Cu matrix, with specific layer definitions (boundary, constant temperature, Cu) in the atomic model. The exact interface physics (e.g., bonding criteria) beyond layer definition is not detailed in the provided spans.

answers.answer: The interface is modeled by setting the lattice types of both the single crystal Cu matrix and the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating to be the same (FCC). The model includes specific layer definitions: 0-5 Å as boundary, 5-10 Å as constant temperature, and 10-55 Å as Cu.
answers.material: Cu matrix / FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating
answers.processing_state: single crystal FCC / single crystal FCC, as-built atomic model
answers.conditions: vacuum, 300 ps loading + 300 ps unloading, 300 K-1200 K
answers.measurement_outcome: defined simulation layers with consistent lattice types
answers.mechanism: FCC lattice matching for both materials in the atomic model
answers.boundary_limitation: Virtual indenter interaction defined by fixed force law
evidence_spans: In the nanoindentation model, single crystal Cu was used as the matrix material and FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as the coating material.
The same lattice types of both materials were set.
The model size of the Cu matrix was 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å, and the total number of atoms was 47,111.

source_evidence_spans: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as a coating material to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix.
